security_audit.summary: Most static matches are documentation syntax, intended HTTPS service calls, or protected token storage; no evidence found of prompt injection or covert credential harvesting. Legacy transport implementations and examples expose reusable tokens despite explicit opt-in. API URL overrides also permit credential-bearing HTTP requests without that opt-in; remote services and dependency behavior were not independently verified.

remediation.issue: Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT transmit reusable proxy credentials without encryption.
remediation.suggestion: Remove legacy credential transports or require an independently encrypted channel. Retain TLS certificate verification and prohibit automatic downgrade.

remediation.issue: Environment URL overrides can bypass the credential transport safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS for credential-bearing API requests and enforce curl protocol restrictions. Reject insecure overrides before reading or sending credentials.

content.user_title: Manage x402socks Proxy Access and Payments
content.value_statement: Regional proxy access requires payment approval, credential protection, and reliable connection checks. This skill provides x402 purchase guidance and helpers for quoting, token management, and egress testing.
actual_capabilities: Check service health, list available exit nodes, and inspect live package prices and entitlements.
Decode live payment challenges and compare quoted amounts against a configured USDC maximum.
Provide TypeScript payment policies and Python validation sketches for checking approved terms before signing.
Save tokens with restricted permissions and atomically replace credentials during rotation or recovery.
Validate tokens, inspect account usage, and test egress through a selected TLS CONNECT exit.
Provide proxy configuration examples for curl, Python, Node, Playwright, and Chrome.
limitations: Purchases require explicitly approved spending, a funded Base wallet, and a separate payment client; the helper does not execute purchases.
Exit availability, TLS support, package prices, and entitlements can change; documentation tables are snapshots.
Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable credentials; quotas, session limits, and fair-use restrictions also apply.
Python payment examples require signer integration and signing-time validation; the supplied sketch is not a complete purchasing client.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Application Behavior
use_cases.description: Select a healthy regional exit and confirm egress before testing an application that you are authorized to assess.

use_cases.title: Budget Agent Proxy Access
use_cases.description: Review live package terms and enforce approved payment requirements before giving an agent paid proxy access.

use_cases.title: Maintain Proxy Credentials
use_cases.description: Diagnose token failures, rotate exposed credentials, and recover access after a settled payment without purchasing again.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Available Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks health, available exits, and current packages. Summarize the results without accessing my wallet or making a purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote time_6h with a maximum of 1.00 USDC. Present all payment terms for approval. Do not sign or pay.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a live quote before authorization.

prompt_templates.title: Test Protected Egress
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing token file to validate access and test eu-north1 through TLS CONNECT. Keep credentials out of arguments and output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify an existing account and selected exit.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Payment Guards
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the TypeScript example to my approved scheme, network, asset, recipient, domain, and amount. Reject mismatches before signing. Do not execute a payment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: integrate guarded purchasing into an existing client.

output_examples.input: Explain the purchase approval checks without buying access.
output_examples.output: Approval review: record the package, maximum amount, network, asset, recipient, and asset domain. Check the signing challenge against those terms. Stop on mismatches.

output_examples.input: Explain how to handle a settled payment that returned no usable token.
output_examples.output: Recovery plan: retain the settlement transaction hash and use the paying wallet to sign the recovery message. Submit recovery without another purchase. Store the replacement privately.

output_examples.input: Explain which proxy transport protects authentication.
output_examples.output: Transport recommendation: use a healthy TLS CONNECT exit with certificate verification enabled. Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose the reusable token. Do not silently downgrade.

best_practices: Approve complete payment terms and enforce them against the requirement being signed, not only a preliminary catalog quote.
Keep tokens in private files, avoid credential-bearing arguments and logs, and rotate credentials after suspected exposure.
Use verified TLS endpoints, refresh node availability, and recover settled purchases instead of paying again.
anti_patterns: Allowing an unattended payment wrapper to sign changed requirements without checking the approved asset, recipient, domain, and amount.
Placing tokens in chat, source control, command arguments, or plaintext proxy connections on untrusted networks.
Treating a changed IP as permission to bypass access restrictions, or as proof of complete anonymity.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Executing the helper requires a client with shell access.

faq.question: What software and funds are required?
faq.answer: The helper uses Bash, curl, and Python 3. Purchasing also requires a payment client and an approved wallet with USDC on Base.

faq.question: Does the shell helper purchase access automatically?
faq.answer: No. It quotes challenges and manages existing credentials. Purchase instructions use separate payment libraries and require explicit authorization.

faq.question: Are all proxy transports encrypted?
faq.answer: No. TLS CONNECT protects authentication when certificates are verified. SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose tokens and require explicit opt-in in the helper.

faq.question: Can access be recovered after losing the token?
faq.answer: The documented recovery flow uses the settlement transaction hash and a fresh signature from the paying wallet. Recovery depends on account eligibility.

faq.question: Does a proxy guarantee anonymity or access?
faq.answer: No. It changes the visible egress IP. Provider trust, target restrictions, browser identifiers, and transport configuration still matter.
